en: He walked among his people and was honored
He mounted a charger for the poor
Kozoy understood the people
If you are a hero who will go
Two days from two young ones
Let your many souls take heed
One falcon among many eagles
Kinsmen stood without parting
Letting his swan-white hair trail
His mirror-bright eyes reddened
His eyes narrowed like a snake’s
If you remain, the word remains
Thirty brave hearts were joined
Kozoy goes before the purpose is complete
In life he has no people
When the Kazakh rejoice over spoils
This too becomes steel in fire
The undying hero brings news
We suffered in this world
Let blood answer blood
I will bear it with sorrow
Finding a voice through courage
Asking where his age had gone
Did you not say hero Manas stands
His dark fate comes from God
If he is a cursed, wretched soul
Make known the one who struck
A shadow fell across the moonlike face
God created courage
From the hero who dug the black earth
Seven brave hearts grieved
From heroine Saykal herself
Dust was taken from the mountain
A pure wish was made
The sword drew blood from the heart
What he took did not remain
Set your intention and go among the people
Know it; God, give news
He poured blood into the dark water
He wore a coat with a black sash
Where was the fallen shield taken
There is the cherished one called Kenen
That one is my tiger
That Kozoy belongs with you
If you go to Kenen, you will mend
What would he say upon arriving
If you are the honored elder woman
That hero Kenen is the man
Go to Kenen, that very one
Entrusting and assigning it to me
That Chinese hero is the man
Ten voices spoke of Manas
If you unite them, that is the hero
Thus spoke an old woman
She wept before Kyzbег
You saw him among a thousand
Turning the tassel back again
He will set them on the straight road
At midnight, Kenen’s
Making his name known
Of Manas whose spirit rose
You did not understand, make it known
Now hear it, my lady
Holding this ear
Truly, I shall go with knowledge
Appearing in the place of service
Doing the work, he matured
Hearing counsel from those who know the people
Taking heart from the wise
Hearing authority from a hero
His soul was bound to the age
He stood burning with passion
Sleepless like a vigilant builder
When night came, he took no rest
While resting once, he heard a word
At night he mounted for the enemy road
Hearing that Kenen had come out
At the base of the white steel
At the side of the lion hero
He is a marked champion
Saying Kantay asked after Kozoy
Appearing in his dream
Saying the moonlike Kozoy was sought
Becoming a khan as though destined
Becoming a soul of Kökötöy
With majesty, sword, and courage
One with the ancestral spirit among the people
The homeland grew heated in speech
Saying he carried off my thought
A champion amid grief
Saying, I saw the enemy at night
The hour came for life to part
Saying, my strength is beyond measure
One brave retainer came forth
From here onward he forgot
The wrestlers gathered
It became long and drawn out
They questioned in return
It passed beyond ninety
A man who knew forty things arose
The steadfast lord’s way of life,
The blunt marksman Bekturmush,
Who inhabited Ala-Too,
A hero and marksman when shots rang out,
Whose skill stirred the people,
Who would not heed a spoken command,
Whose honor would not let his hand be stayed,
Never satisfied in matters of inquiry,
Never abandoning his ardor,
Dwelling upon Ala-Too,
Facing the enemy host toward Beijing,
Inhabiting a courageous land,
Bowing his head before Chyngyz,
A venomous force against flying bullets,
A precious breed of lion,
If met, surpassing any living soul,
Meeting others, he carried their secrets,
Which hero could merely stand watching,
When roused, the lion would seize,
He would cleave the black mountain,
He was the hero of the dear people,
The hero’s remaining hope,
If you are his companion, honor him,
A retainer who gladdens the soul,
If you take your young one, that is the hero’s intent,
The bay horse had a singular form,
He brought forth aid beneath the sun,
It proved skittish from behind,
Measured among ten champions,
Wise was what he said,
He never held back the words in his mouth,
Bowing to whomever he encountered,
A fierce hero who showed no favor,
Aykanysh had heard it,
The people were gathered in that place,
Saying he was apart in battle,
She spoke of four, then said one alone,
She spoke of the stratagem she sought,
Thus had she heard it,
Speaking of the day’s design,
He did not come every full day,
The falcon Kenen for all time,
None among the people remained whole,
Led by the fierce falcon,
None on earth remained untouched,
This Kenen did not abandon his cause,
No hero remained whole,
She said truly that his equal remained,
No person had seen what Heaven saw,
Let no rivals approach him,
There is no equal in the world.
Hearing this, Aykanysh,
She too loosed an arrow,
She undertook the task for twelve thousand,
My camel-eyed one beyond arrow’s reach,
Each day the lion’s mount,
The day for shedding blood had come,
His boots unseen by any soul,
Hanging whip and sword upon himself,
Girding his slender waist,
Drawing an iron coat over his body,
Broad-chested, with a mountain heart,
A hero bold of speech,
The ages produced none to match him,
They would make him leader of a hundred,
The black musket was fearsome,
It sharpened their courage,
The black earth did not split apart,
It thundered as though the land surged,
Stirring his white beard,
His specially learned mullah,
The palace that governed the people,
Making them serve the hero,
Driving grief from the people,
The finest came to the horde,
Leaving the horde, he rallied the people,
He would tell everything to the people,
From the hands of the wearied province,
He would leave them unharmed,
His life endured four days of trial,
The people’s vast lineage,
The entrusted tribute,
Gathering all the people,
The legacy mounted by the pasha,
Ask nothing of the inheritance,
The heirloom’s thoroughbred,
For this entire host was stern,
For this whole multitude was wondrous,
The mounted people were renowned,
The heroes ran and assembled,
All day long they met,
The gathered people recited at home,
Cloudlike, they surged in alarm,
The children of the people made ready,
Preparing to fight the unruly host,
All the people ran together,
Those of sound mind did not stay behind,
Those ignorant from of old,
Wondering how many people would go,
The people grieved and stood immense,
Young boys ran about,
The champions who staked their lives,
Were chosen for the mass contest,
Mounting up and drawing level,
The people cried out and the nation stirred,
The khan’s camp thundered,
Kabay cast on his great coat,
His rounded garment bulging,
Ask not of his lament,
Aykanysh in the lofty tower,
Her two thousand put on their gear,
Saying the road had opened,
Restless souls appeared,
When she sent the wretched one into sorrow,
The course of the road became known,
Donning many a gold robe,
His falconlike form appeared,
Straining like a blue-gray stallion,
Those they loved were content at heart,
When found, he understood,
A hero mounted upon three steeds,
His remaining keen sword,
The watching people stirred,
From the world where his life lay,
His ambition began to rise,
What this courageous one knew,
The courageous need a people,
And the good men, without exception,
A courage-less gossip,
When a holy campaign begins,
When an uproar rises among your people,
With your foremost elder as the banner,
If he appears a hero from youth,
If he encircles all who act,
Submitting to a single treasury,
Souls apart [?],
The dark ravine, the dense [?],
The dark one thirsting to drink blood,
Champions who gathered their weapons,
Without talking much or uttering words,
The people's worthy man is a pure man.
All the people submitted,
If there is an enemy, his true companion,
Putting on battle dress,
There is a champion, one or two,
From the wretch who listened to gossip,
Is there a single word from his offspring?
When the people stir, without making war,
A man whose courage is lofty,
Courage, poor wretch, the people's support,
Without making his body wolf-like with a sword,
All valor becoming practiced,
The whole world becomes accustomed,
Would the mind not be overwhelmed?
A commander of troops, a leader of men,
An equal man who speaks fully,
